label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I q.2 a.2…: In proving from his effects that God exists, the…
locator: I q.2 a.2 ad 2: accipere possumus pro medio quid significet hoc nomen Deus
interpretation: When a cause is demonstrated from its effect, the effect takes the place of the cause's definition; to prove that something exists, one takes as the middle what the name signifies, not what the thing is, because the question what it is follows the question whether it is. The names of God are imposed from his effects, so in proving from an effect that God exists one may take as middle what the name 'God' signifies. This is why the five ways may end with a nominal definition (et hoc dicimus Deum). Not formalized: it bears on the nominal definition without stating it.
